title.justification: The paper's focus is on the hypothesis proposed, which is that maximizing reward is sufficient to drive intelligent behavior in both natural and artificial intelligence.
title.quote: In this article we hypothesise that intelligence, and its associated abilities, can be understood as subserving the maximisation of reward.

analysis.description: This paper proposes the 'Reward is Enough' hypothesis, suggesting that the maximization of reward can explain and drive intelligent behavior in both natural and artificial systems, potentially leading to artificial general intelligence. The authors argue that diverse abilities like knowledge, learning, perception, and language can arise through the pursuit of rewards, making specialized problem formulations unnecessary for each ability.

type.justification: The paper is focused on proposing a hypothesis and discussing its implications rather than conducting empirical experiments or providing experimental results.
type.quote: We have presented the reward-is-enough hypothesis and some of its implications.

name.justification: The paper discusses reinforcement learning as a central theme, proposing that reward maximization can lead to general intelligence.
name.quote: One might then expect to find such methods in natural intelligence, or choose to implement them in artificial intelligence. Among possible methods for maximising reward, the most general and scalable approach is to learn to do so, by interacting with the environment by trial and error.

name.justification: The paper discusses the possibility of achieving artificial general intelligence through reinforcement learning and reward maximization.
name.quote: ...therefore that powerful reinforcement learning agents could constitute a solution to artificial general intelligence.

name.justification: AlphaZero is mentioned as an example of a model that follows the reward maximization approach.
name.quote: AlphaZero’s abilities were innately integrated into a unified whole, whereas integration had proven highly problematic in prior work.

is_contributed.justification: The paper discusses AlphaZero as an existing example reinforcing the hypothesis rather than a new contribution.
is_contributed.quote: Research initially focused largely upon distinct abilities... AlphaZero focused instead on a singular goal: maximising a reward signal...

is_executed.justification: AlphaZero, which is discussed in the paper, is known to have been executed on GPUs.
is_executed.quote: AlphaZero’s abilities were innately integrated into a unified whole...

is_compared.justification: The paper compares AlphaZero’s performance and abilities achieved through reward maximization to previous models.
is_compared.quote: AlphaZero learned (see Section 1) an integrated intelligence across many facets of Go.
